meta.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
meta.author: bank-team-web-development
meta.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.learningObjective: Identify the DOM as a tree structure
questions.stem: In a study group revision, the DOM is best described as which structure?

options.text: A tree of nodes with parent-child relationships
A flat list of tags in source order

questions.explanation: The DOM represents the document as a tree where elements are nodes connected by parent-child relationships. Source order alone ignores nesting.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.learningObjective: Predict parsing of a block inside a paragraph
questions.stem: A study group revision asks what happens when a div is nested inside a p. Which outcome is correct?

options.text: The div nests normally inside p
The browser closes the p before the div

questions.explanation: A p cannot contain block-level content. The parser implicitly closes the p before the div, splitting the paragraph.

questions.topic: Display decides block or inline, not the tag name
questions.learningObjective: Explain that display controls layout role
questions.stem: In a study group revision, which property determines whether an element is block or inline?
questions.explanation: Layout role comes from CSS display, not the tag. A span can be display:block and a div inline.

questions.topic: Choosing an element for what it means rather than how it looks
questions.learningObjective: Choose semantic elements over presentational ones
questions.stem: A study group revision wants a page title. Which element is most appropriate?

options.text: span with inline style for size
div with large font because it looks big
b because it makes text bold
h1 because it denotes a top-level heading

questions.explanation: Choosing by meaning keeps structure accessible and styleable. Presentational hacks lose semantics.

questions.topic: What a heading outline with a skipped level claims
questions.learningObjective: Identify the issue with skipped heading levels
questions.stem: A study group revision sees an outline h1 then h3. What problem does this raise?

options.text: It changes the visual size only
It skips a structural level in the outline
It makes the page invalid HTML
It hides the heading from search engines

questions.explanation: Skipping h2 breaks the heading outline hierarchy. It is valid HTML but harms accessibility and structure.

questions.topic: Heading levels are structure rather than size
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish heading level from font size
questions.stem: In a study group revision, heading levels primarily convey what?
questions.explanation: Heading levels encode structure and outline. Visual size is a separate CSS concern.

questions.topic: What a form actually submits
questions.stem: A study group revision asks what a form submits by default. Which answer is correct?
questions.explanation: Forms submit successful controls as name-value pairs, encoded per method and enctype.

questions.topic: Collapsing a run of white space in ordinary text
questions.stem:
A study group revision renders `

a b

`. How does the text display?
questions.explanation: In normal flow, runs of whitespace collapse to a single space. Leading and trailing spaces are also trimmed.

questions.topic: The outer width under the initial box-sizing
questions.learningObjective: Compute outer width with default box-sizing
questions.stem: A study group revision has an element width 100px, padding 10px each side, border 2px each side, default box-sizing. What is the outer width?
questions.explanation: Default content-box: outer width = 100 + 2*10 + 2*2 = 124px. Padding and border add outside.
questions.hint: Add padding and border both sides.

questions.topic: The content width under border-box sizing
questions.stem: A study group revision uses border-box with width 100px, padding 10px each side, border 2px each side. What is the content width?
questions.explanation: Border-box: content width = 100 - 2*10 - 2*2 = 76px. Padding and border are included in width.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish DOM tree from text sequence
questions.stem: A study group revision compares DOM to source text. Which statement is true?

options.text: DOM is a flat token list
DOM is a parsed tree, not raw text

questions.explanation: The DOM is a parsed in-memory tree. It may differ from raw source due to normalization and error recovery.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.learningObjective: Identify the resulting DOM after auto-closing
questions.stem:
A study group revision parses `

text

x

`. How many p elements result?
questions.explanation:
The p closes before the div, leaving one p with text. The trailing

is ignored as stray.

questions.topic: Display decides block or inline, not the tag name
questions.learningObjective: Predict layout of a span set to block
questions.stem: A study group revision sets `span { display:block; }`. How does the span behave?

options.text: It stays inline because span is inline
It generates a block box and breaks lines

questions.explanation: display:block makes the span a block box regardless of tag name, causing line breaks.

questions.topic: Choosing an element for what it means rather than how it looks
questions.learningObjective: Pick a semantic element for navigation
questions.stem: A study group revision needs a site navigation block. Which element fits?

options.text: div with links because it works

questions.explanation: nav conveys navigation semantics to assistive tech and search engines. A generic div loses that meaning.

questions.topic: What a heading outline with a skipped level claims
questions.stem: A study group revision outline is h1, h2, h2, h3. Is the outline sound?
questions.explanation: Repeating h2 and stepping to h3 by one is valid. Skipping levels, not repeating, is the problem.

questions.topic: Heading levels are structure rather than size
questions.stem: A study group revision asks why heading levels should reflect document structure instead of visual size. Explain.

answer.exemplar: Heading levels encode the document outline and nesting, so assistive technologies and search engines can navigate sections; visual size should be controlled with CSS independently.

questions.explanation: Heading levels define outline and nesting for accessibility and SEO. Visual size is a presentation concern handled by CSS.

questions.topic: What a form actually submits
questions.stem: A study group revision has an unchecked checkbox. Is it submitted?

options.text: No, unchecked checkboxes are not successful

questions.explanation: Only successful controls are submitted. An unchecked checkbox is not successful and is omitted.

questions.topic: Collapsing a run of white space in ordinary text
questions.stem: A study group revision sets `white-space:nowrap`. What happens to spaces in text?

options.text: Spaces still collapse but text does not wrap

questions.explanation: nowrap collapses whitespace like normal but prevents line wrapping. pre preserves spaces and prevents wrapping.

questions.topic: The outer width under the initial box-sizing
questions.stem: A study group revision has width 80px, padding 5px each side, border 1px each side, default box-sizing. What is the outer width?
questions.explanation: Content-box outer width = 80 + 2*5 + 2*1 = 92px.

questions.topic: The content width under border-box sizing
questions.stem: A study group revision uses border-box with width 80px, padding 5px each side, border 1px each side. What is the content width?
questions.explanation: Border-box content width = 80 - 2*5 - 2*1 = 68px.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.stem:
A study group revision has `

x

`. What is the parent of the p element?
questions.explanation: The p is directly nested in the div, so div is its parent node in the DOM tree.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.stem:
A study group revision writes `

Hello

world

`. What is the parse result?

options.text: p contains both Hello and div
p contains Hello, then div is a sibling

questions.explanation:
The p closes at the div, so Hello stays in p and div becomes a sibling. The closing

is ignored.

questions.topic: Display decides block or inline, not the tag name
questions.learningObjective: Identify default display of a div
questions.stem: A study group revision asks the default display of a div. What is it?
questions.explanation: A div defaults to display:block. Tag names carry default display, but CSS can override it.

questions.topic: Choosing an element for what it means rather than how it looks
questions.stem: A study group revision needs to mark a block quotation. Which element fits?

options.text: blockquote because it denotes a quotation

questions.explanation: blockquote carries quotation semantics and default indentation. Presentational styling alone loses meaning.

questions.topic: What a heading outline with a skipped level claims
questions.stem: A study group revision outline is h1, h3. What is wrong?

options.text: It skips h2, breaking the outline

questions.explanation: Skipping from h1 to h3 omits a level, weakening the outline. It is valid HTML but poor structure.

questions.topic: Heading levels are structure rather than size
questions.learningObjective: Explain why not to choose heading by size
questions.stem: A study group revision asks why choosing a heading level for its font size is wrong. Explain.

answer.exemplar: Heading levels define document outline and accessibility; using them for size conflates structure with presentation and misleads assistive technologies.

questions.explanation: Heading levels encode outline and accessibility. Choosing by size conflates structure with presentation and misleads assistive tech.

questions.topic: What a form actually submits
questions.stem: A study group revision has a disabled input. Is it submitted?

options.text: No, disabled controls are not successful

questions.explanation: Disabled controls are not successful and are omitted from submission. Use readonly if the value must submit.

questions.topic: Collapsing a run of white space in ordinary text
questions.stem: A study group revision uses `white-space:pre`. How are multiple spaces rendered?
questions.explanation: pre preserves whitespace and prevents wrapping. Multiple spaces remain visible.

questions.topic: The outer width under the initial box-sizing
questions.stem: A study group revision has width 60px, padding 4px each side, border 3px each side, default box-sizing. What is the outer width?
questions.explanation: Content-box outer width = 60 + 2*4 + 2*3 = 74px.

questions.topic: The content width under border-box sizing
questions.stem: A study group revision uses border-box with width 60px, padding 4px each side, border 3px each side. What is the content width?
questions.explanation: Border-box content width = 60 - 2*4 - 2*3 = 46px.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.stem: A study group revision asks the root of an HTML document tree. What is it?
questions.explanation: The document node is the root of the DOM tree; html is its document element child.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.learningObjective: Explain why p cannot contain div
questions.stem: A study group revision asks why a p cannot contain a div. Explain.

answer.exemplar: The content model of p allows only phrasing content, so a block-level div forces the parser to close the paragraph before the div.

questions.explanation: p's content model allows phrasing content only. A block-level div forces the parser to close the p first.

questions.topic: Display decides block or inline, not the tag name
questions.stem: A study group revision asks the default display of a span. What is it?
questions.explanation: A span defaults to display:inline. CSS can change it to block or other values.

questions.topic: Choosing an element for what it means rather than how it looks
questions.stem: A study group revision needs an unordered list of items. Which element fits?
questions.explanation: ul with li conveys list semantics, enabling assistive tech navigation and default styling.

questions.topic: What a heading outline with a skipped level claims
questions.stem: A study group revision outline is h1, h4. What is the issue?

options.text: It skips two levels, harming structure
Only h2 is allowed after h1

questions.explanation: Skipping multiple levels weakens the outline. It remains valid HTML but is poor structure.

questions.topic: Heading levels are structure rather than size
questions.stem: A study group revision has an h2 section. Its subsection should use which level?

options.text: h3 because it is one level deeper

questions.explanation: A subsection under h2 should be h3, one level deeper, preserving outline nesting.

questions.topic: What a form actually submits
questions.stem: A study group revision has `<button>Save</button>` inside a form. What does it do?
questions.explanation: A button defaults to type=submit inside a form, triggering submission.

questions.topic: Collapsing a run of white space in ordinary text
questions.stem: A study group revision asks the default white-space value for normal text. What is it?
questions.explanation: The default is white-space:normal, which collapses whitespace and wraps text.

questions.topic: The outer width under the initial box-sizing
questions.stem: A study group revision assumes width sets the outer width by default. What is wrong?

options.text: Width ignores padding but includes border
Default box-sizing is content-box, so width excludes padding and border

questions.explanation: By default box-sizing is content-box, so width covers only content. Padding and border add to the outer width.

questions.topic: The content width under border-box sizing
questions.stem: A study group revision asks why border-box makes layout easier. Explain.

answer.exemplar: Border-box includes padding and border in the declared width, so the element's outer width matches the specified value and layouts stay predictable.

questions.explanation: Border-box includes padding and border in width, making the declared width the actual outer width and simplifying layout math.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.stem:
A study group revision has `
  • a
  • b
`. What is the nextSibling of the first li?
questions.explanation: The first li's nextSibling is the second li, ignoring whitespace text nodes in simplified view.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.stem: A study group revision asks stage one: what happens to a div nested in a p during parsing?

options.text: The p closes before the div

questions.explanation: The parser auto-closes the p before the div, so the div becomes a sibling rather than a child.

questions.topic: Display decides block or inline, not the tag name
questions.stem: A study group revision asks how a div can behave like an inline element. Explain.

answer.exemplar: Setting display:inline on a div makes it generate an inline box, so layout role follows CSS rather than the tag name.

questions.explanation: CSS display overrides the default layout role. A div with display:inline behaves inline.

questions.topic: Choosing an element for what it means rather than how it looks
questions.stem: A study group revision wants to emphasize a word semantically. Which element fits?
questions.explanation: em conveys emphasis semantics. i and b are presentational; span with style loses meaning.

questions.topic: What a heading outline with a skipped level claims
questions.stem: A study group revision asks the main harm of skipping heading levels. Which is it?

options.text: It weakens the document outline for assistive tech

questions.explanation: Skipped levels harm outline navigation for assistive technologies. The HTML remains valid.

questions.topic: Heading levels are structure rather than size
questions.stem: A study group revision asks stage one: what does an h2 represent?
questions.explanation: h2 denotes a second-level section in the document outline, independent of its rendered size.

questions.topic: What a form actually submits
questions.stem: A study group revision has a file input. What must the form use to submit files?
questions.explanation: File uploads require POST with multipart/form-data. GET cannot carry file bodies.

questions.topic: Collapsing a run of white space in ordinary text
questions.stem: A study group revision sets a flex container. Does whitespace between items collapse?

options.text: Whitespace text nodes are ignored in flex layout

questions.explanation: Flex layout ignores whitespace-only text nodes between flex items, so no extra gaps appear.

questions.topic: The outer width under the initial box-sizing
questions.stem: A study group revision has width 50px, padding 2px each side, border 1px each side, margin 3px each side, default box-sizing. What is the outer width including margin?
questions.explanation: Outer width including margin = 50 + 2*2 + 2*1 + 2*3 = 62px.

questions.topic: The content width under border-box sizing
questions.stem: A study group revision uses border-box with width 50px, padding 2px each side, border 1px each side, margin 3px each side. What is the content width?
questions.explanation: Border-box content width = 50 - 2*2 - 2*1 = 44px. Margin is outside and does not affect content width.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.stem: A study group revision asks why changing the DOM updates the page. Explain.

answer.exemplar: The browser renders from the DOM tree, so mutating nodes changes the rendered output without reloading the source document.

questions.explanation: The browser renders from the DOM tree. Mutating it updates the rendered page without reloading source.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.stem: A study group revision asks which nesting is invalid. Which is it?
questions.explanation: p cannot contain block-level elements like div. Phrasing elements such as span, strong, and a are allowed.

questions.topic: Display decides block or inline, not the tag name
questions.learningObjective: Predict display of a custom element
questions.stem: A study group revision defines a custom element with no CSS. How does it display by default?

options.text: inline because unknown elements default to inline

questions.explanation: Unknown elements default to display:inline in HTML. Custom elements without defined display follow this default.

questions.topic: Choosing an element for what it means rather than how it looks
questions.stem: A study group revision needs an image with a caption. Which element fits?
questions.explanation: figure with figcaption semantically groups media with its caption.

questions.topic: What a heading outline with a skipped level claims
questions.stem: A study group revision asks stage one: does a skipped heading level affect rendering?

options.text: No, rendering depends on CSS not outline

questions.explanation: Skipped levels do not affect rendering. They harm outline and accessibility, not visual layout.

questions.topic: Heading levels are structure rather than size
questions.stem: A study group revision asks whether multiple h1 elements are allowed. What is correct?

options.text: No, only one h1 per page
Yes, HTML allows multiple h1 elements

questions.explanation: HTML permits multiple h1 elements. Best practice varies, but it is not invalid.

questions.topic: What a form actually submits
questions.stem: A study group revision asks the default form method. What is it?
questions.explanation: The default form method is GET. Data appears in the URL query string unless method=POST is set.

questions.topic: Collapsing a run of white space in ordinary text
questions.stem: A study group revision asks which element preserves whitespace by default. Which is it?
questions.explanation: pre preserves whitespace and prevents wrapping. p, div, and span collapse whitespace.

questions.topic: The outer width under the initial box-sizing
questions.stem: A study group revision has width 40px, no padding, no border, default box-sizing. What is the outer width?
questions.explanation: With no padding or border, content-box outer width equals the declared width of 40px.

questions.topic: The content width under border-box sizing
questions.stem: A study group revision uses border-box with width 40px, no padding, no border. What is the content width?
questions.explanation: With no padding or border, border-box content width equals the declared width of 40px.
